rationale: Identity was verified correctly via full name and zip, matched to a single user account. The agent pulled the user’s recent orders and identified the delivered camera. They checked product variants with the read-only tool, presented only available higher-zoom options, and the user explicitly chose the 30MP, 10x, SD variant. Before making any write, the agent asked which payment method to use for the price difference; the user specified PayPal. The agent then executed the exchange using the correct order and item IDs, set the payment method to the user’s PayPal, and the tool confirmed status changed to “exchange requested” with the correct price difference ($170.68). Final messaging accurately described the result and next steps. No unsupported claims, wrong-user actions, or unconfirmed writes occurred. While the selected item changed resolution from 24MP to 30MP, the user explicitly chose that option, and policy requirements were met.
